mutable_state.name: reservation record
mutable_state.lifecycle: Absent -> inserted within transaction -> committed; a failed transaction returns to Absent.
mutable_state.mutability: Rows are created by POST /reservations; this API exposes no update or delete transition.

mutable_state.name: resource occupancy
mutable_state.storage: Derived from committed reservation rows; not a separate mutable record.
mutable_state.lifecycle: Changes only when a reservation commits.
mutable_state.mutability: The resource-scoped transaction lock serializes the overlap-check and insert critical section.

mutable_state.name: idempotency binding
mutable_state.storage: The unique idempotency_key column on the reservation row.
mutable_state.lifecycle: Unused -> bound to one committed reservation; an exact replay reads and returns that binding without writing.
mutable_state.mutability: A key cannot be rebound to a different payload; the database unique constraint and key-scoped lock serialize creation.

mutable_state.name: transaction-scoped locks
mutable_state.storage: PostgreSQL advisory transaction locks; ephemeral, not committed application state.
mutable_state.lifecycle: Acquired during the transaction and released on commit or rollback.

dependencies.role: Reject malformed or out-of-bounds request fields before database mutation.
Require timezone-aware timestamps and normalize instants to UTC before ordering, idempotency comparison, and persistence.
Make overlap check and insert atomic; exceptions must roll back pending writes.
Serialize concurrent overlap-check/insert paths for the same resource.

dependencies.component: idempotency-scoped advisory transaction lock and UNIQUE constraint
dependencies.role: Serialize same-key lookups and guarantee at most one committed row per key, including requests for different resources.

dependencies.component: reservations table CHECK and timestamptz columns
dependencies.role: Enforce end_at > start_at at storage and persist absolute instants.
Exercise concurrency, replay/key reuse, timezone equivalence, and invalid-input/no-state-change behavior against a running service.

invariants.statement: For any two committed reservations A and B with the same resource_id, their half-open intervals [start_at, end_at) are disjoint: A.end_at <= B.start_at or B.end_at <= A.start_at. Adjacent reservations are legal.
enforcement_basis: Resource-scoped transaction lock covers the overlap query and insert.
Overlap predicate is existing.start_at < requested.end_at AND requested.start_at < existing.end_at.
invariants.witness: Run the concurrent conflicting-reservations attack; assert no two overlapping requests for one resource both commit, and assert adjacent intervals can both commit.

invariants.statement: Each committed Idempotency-Key maps to exactly one canonical request payload and at most one reservation. Replaying that key with the same resource_id, UTC start_at, UTC end_at, and guest_name returns the original reservation id without another insert; changing any payload field is rejected without changing state.
enforcement_basis: Existing key is compared against all request fields before replay.
invariants.witness: Run same-key concurrent/replay and key-reuse cases; assert a stable reservation id and row count for exact replay, and HTTP 409 with unchanged rows for different payload.

invariants.statement: Timezone-aware datetime values denoting the same instant have identical canonical UTC values and therefore produce identical interval, overlap, and idempotency comparisons, independent of their input offsets.
enforcement_basis: canonical_utc converts aware request timestamps to timezone.utc before database access.
invariants.witness: Run UTC and non-zero-offset representations of the same interval; assert same-key replay returns the original id and equivalent instants are not treated as distinct availability.

invariants.statement: Invalid input, key-reuse rejection, overlap rejection, or a failed transaction must not leave any committed reservation or idempotency binding from that attempt.
enforcement_basis: Request and interval validation precede reservation insertion.
The overlap check and insert run inside one transaction.
Raised HTTPException or database exceptions abort pending transactional writes.
invariants.witness: Snapshot reservations before and after invalid/missing-timezone/reversed-interval attempts and injected transaction failure; assert HTTP rejection and no new row or key binding.
